claims.text: The novel refractory material is solid at room temperature.
Adaptive bias force can be implemented in an ab initio DFT free-energy approach for refractory-material melting calculations.
Metadynamics can be implemented in an ab initio DFT free-energy approach for refractory-material melting calculations.
Advanced sampling increases the sampling efficiency of free-energy calculations.
Increased sampling efficiency reduces the computational cost of thermodynamic integration.
The proposed approach can calculate the melting temperature of novel refractory materials within 10% of experiment.
The proposed approach can calculate the entropy of fusion within 5% of experiment.
The proposed approach can calculate the enthalpy of fusion within 10% of experiment.
The proposed approach can calculate the volume change at the melting point within 5% of experiment.
The proposed approach reduces computational cost by at least 50% relative to a traditional ab initio DFT free-energy approach.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the implementation of the advanced sampling technique.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the quality of the underlying DFT calculations.
A deviation greater than 15% from experiment for any measured melting property is defined as a falsifying outcome.
